text: We like Marcus none the worse for this spice of mischief. Another letter describes a visit to a country town, and shows the antiquarian spirit of the writer:— 'M. CÆSAR to his MASTER M. FRONTO, greeting. 'After I entered the carriage, after I took leave of you, we made a journey comfortable enough, but we had a few drops of rain to wet us. But before coming to the country-house, we broke our journey at Anagnia, a mile or so from the highroad.
